# Data Safety Requirements Checklist: GymTracker v1

**Purpose**: Validate that requirements governing destructive and irreversible operations — the demo reset, archiving, deletion of historical records, and failure recovery — are complete, explicit, and leave no unrecoverable behavior undefined.
**Created**: 2026-09-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the exact scope of "all existing application data" enumerated for the demo reset, including user-created exercises, foods, and goal sets? [Completeness, Spec §FR-041] — resolved by FR-041c, which names all seven tables
- [x] CHK002 Is the confirmation mechanism for the reset specified as a requirement, or only as a contract detail? [Gap, Spec §FR-041a vs Contract §Demo] — resolved by FR-041d
- [x] CHK003 Are atomicity requirements defined for the reset, so a mid-operation failure cannot leave the database partially wiped? [Gap, Recovery Flow] — resolved by FR-041e
- [x] CHK004 Are recovery requirements defined for a failed or interrupted destructive operation? [Gap, Exception Flow] — resolved by FR-041e: atomicity makes recovery unnecessary, since the database is never left mid-change
- [x] CHK005 Is the permission to hard-delete an unreferenced exercise or food stated as a requirement, or only as an assumption? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions vs §FR-004b] — resolved by FR-004c
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for what happens to a session's sets when the session is deleted? [Gap, Spec §FR-010] — resolved by FR-010a
- [x] CHK007 Are confirmation requirements defined for non-reset destructive actions — deleting a session, body weight entry, meal entry, or goal set? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, §FR-015, §FR-023] — resolved by FR-038a
- [x] CHK008 Are requirements defined for the behavior when the database file is missing, unreadable, or corrupt at startup? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] — resolved by FR-035a
- [x] CHK009 Is there a requirement restricting network exposure of the destructive reset operation? [Gap, Spec §Requirements vs Plan §Constitution Check] — resolved by FR-039a, promoted from the plan into the spec
- [x] CHK010 Are undo or recovery-window requirements defined for any destructive action, or is their absence explicitly recorded as accepted? [Gap] — resolved by FR-038b and §Assumptions "No undo, no backup, no export"

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK011 Is "explicit confirmation" quantified — a typed phrase, a checkbox, a second click? [Clarity, Spec §FR-041a] — resolved by FR-041d (typed, case-sensitive `RESET`) and FR-038a (one step for single-record deletes)
- [x] CHK012 Is "permanently erased" distinguished from archiving clearly enough that a reader cannot confuse the two? [Clarity, Spec §FR-041a, §FR-004] — resolved by FR-004c and FR-041c, which state the two outcomes in non-overlapping terms
- [x] CHK013 Is "excluded from pickers and search by default" precise about which surfaces show archived items and which hide them? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-024b] — resolved by FR-004d, which enumerates both sets of surfaces
- [x] CHK014 Is the warning text requirement specific about what the user must be told before the reset proceeds? [Clarity, Spec §FR-041a] — resolved by FR-041d, which specifies the three facts the warning must convey

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK015 Are archiving requirements for exercises and foods stated symmetrically, with no capability present for one and absent for the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-004a, §FR-024b] — resolved by FR-004c, FR-004d, FR-004e, which are written to apply to both
- [x] CHK016 Is the prohibition on deleting referenced catalog items consistent between the exercise and food requirements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004b, §FR-024b] — resolved by FR-004c stating one rule for both
- [x] CHK017 Does the requirement that seed data behaves identically to user data hold against the reset requirement, which deletes both without distinction? [Consistency, Spec §FR-042, §FR-041] — verified consistent: FR-041c makes the lack of distinction explicit, which is exactly what FR-042 asserts
- [x] CHK018 Do the sample-data requirements and the sample-data assumption agree that no automatic loading occurs under any condition? [Consistency, Spec §FR-043 vs §Assumptions] — verified: both now state the explicit-only rule

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK019 Are requirements defined for a reset invoked against an already-empty database? [Coverage, Spec §FR-041] — resolved by FR-041f
- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for concurrent use from two browser tabs, where one performs a destructive action? [Gap, Coverage] — resolved by FR-039b: unsupported, last write wins, stale tabs recover on refetch
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements defined for unsaved in-progress edits when a destructive operation completes? [Gap, Exception Flow] — resolved by FR-038c and FR-039b
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for archiving the last remaining exercise, leaving none selectable? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases] — resolved by FR-005a
- [x] CHK023 Are restore requirements defined for an archived item whose name now collides with a newly created active item? [Gap, Spec §FR-004a, §FR-002] — resolved by FR-004e
- [x] CHK024 Is the accidental-reset edge case matched by a requirement that mitigates it? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases vs §FR-041a] — resolved by FR-041d and FR-039a

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK025 Can the determinism criterion for repeated resets be objectively evaluated? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008a] — verified: SC-008a compares two runs for byte-identical data, which is directly checkable
- [x] CHK026 Is the claim that archiving changes zero historical values stated precisely enough to be checked? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009a] — verified: "zero historical totals or trend values" is a before/after comparison
- [x] CHK027 Does a success criterion exist covering safe failure of a destructive operation? [Gap, Spec §Success Criteria] — resolved by SC-013

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK028 Is the assumption that no backup or export exists validated against the irreversibility of the reset? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-041] — resolved: §Assumptions "No undo, no backup, no export" states the trade and its justification explicitly
- [x] CHK029 Is the single-user assumption examined for the multi-tab case it does not actually exclude? [Assumption, Spec §FR-039] — resolved by FR-039b and §Assumptions "Single tab"
- [x] CHK030 Is the assumption that losing demo data is harmless stated anywhere a reader would find it before implementing the reset? [Assumption, Gap] — resolved: stated in §Assumptions alongside the irreversibility trade

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
